findings.claim: _check_identity_conflicts now returns owner_name and owner_birth_date_or_ico (PII) for a soft-deleted Person, because the new outerjoin to Person deliberately omits the Person.deleted_at filter that _find_om_ownership_conflicts applies, and _build_om_conflict unconditionally reads those fields from the joined owner.
findings.evidence: wan/api/scan.py:4197; wan/api/scan.py:4203; wan/api/scan.py:4225; wan/api/scan.py:4077; wan/api/scan.py:4086; wan/api/scan.py:4087; tests/integration/test_conflict_contract.py:335
findings.fix: Either filter Person.deleted_at.is_(None) in the identity-gate join too, or, if the identity/ownership divergence is intentionally kept (as the test at tests/integration/test_conflict_contract.py:335 asserts), suppress owner_name/owner_birth_date_or_ico (and cap conflicts to []) when the joined owner is soft-deleted before calling _build_om_conflict, so a caller cannot read a deleted person's name/birth-date-or-ICO through the confirm_session 422 payload.
